newsitem.title: USA: American begins around-the-world balloon flight.
newsitem.headline: American begins around-the-world balloon flight.

text.p: An American lifted off on an around-the-world solo balloon flight late on Monday from Busch Stadium in downtown St. Louis, an expedition spokesman said.

Steve Fossett, 52, a wealthy Colorado-based commodities broker, lifted off at 11:46 p.m. EST (0446 GMT), piloting his "Solo Spirit" balloon out of the stadium and over the Mississippi River, spokesman Bo Kemper said.
"The launch went very smoothly," Kemper said. "It was a beautiful visual."

Fossett's flight is the third attempt in less than a week at an around-the-world balloon trip. It follows recent failures by rival teams in Europe and North Africa to crack one of manned flight's great barriers -- a goal that also eluded Fossett a year ago when his balloon crashed in Canada during a similar attempt.

On Sunday a balloon piloted by Bertrand Piccard and Wim Verstraeten ditched in the Mediterranean six hours after taking off from the Swiss Alps. Fumes from kerosene leaking into the cabin brought down the Swiss team.

Last Wednesday British tycoon Richard Branson and two crew members brought their Virgin Global Challenger balloon down in Algeria less than 24 hours after taking off from Morocco. The craft had suddenly lost lift and plunged.

Unlike the other recent expeditions, American Fossett is flying alone. He already holds a world distance record for a solo balloon flight set in 1995 when he flew from South Korea to Canada. His balloon gets its lift from helium and hot air, as did the Swiss and British craft.

Kemper said Fossett delayed his launch two hours while waiting for 10 mph (16 kph) winds at the top of the stadium to die down. His flight path will take him across Illinois, Kentucky and Tennessee and into North Carolina by early morning, he said.
Jet streams dipping farther south at high speeds during the Northern Hemisphere winter make January a favoured time for such long-distance balloon flights.
